summary.name: Screen Printing is a supplemental design reference in the Printmaking and Craft Materials category. It is not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Screen Printing uses few spot colors, flat ink layers, and strong positive-negative shapes over visible paper. Slight handmade edges support the print look. Ink coverage and overprints carry the image, and smooth gradients stay secondary.
summary.suitableUses: Explicitly suited to bold flat-ink graphics used alone. Source best-for uses include gig posters, festival promos, narrative posters, travel themes, and title sequences. Inferred: concise copy suits word-card motion, while dense explanatory text fits poorly.
summary.limitations: Explicit constraints: keep inks discrete and limited, add no spot colors, and avoid smooth gradient fills. Keep lettering sharp. Motion references apply only when the scene contains the needed phrase, mark, or punctuation, and choosing none is valid. Duration, aspect ratio, resolution, frame rate, and subject are unspecified.
summary.palette: Suggested only when no approved palette is supplied; task or brand colors override it. Tokens: background #F4E9D4 (dominant paper), foreground #233E45 (dark ink, primary text), accent_1 #B95A43 (rust, decorative only). Foreground on background measures 9.452:1. Accent on background measures 3.789:1, so it fails body text. Gradients are disabled.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is not fixed by the style; references are optional: chaptered handoffs (motion-012), narrative steps (motion-015), spot-ink letter swaps (motion-037), punctuation zoom (motion-038), radial burst (motion-039), and hard word cuts (motion-040). The burst's white and dark pieces must map to approved inks. Video state derives from composition time; scroll or pointer input applies only to interactive delivery, and reduced motion shows the completed state.
summary.audio: No audio is specified by the style. Task-dependent options include restrained music for pacing, voiceover for explanation, sound effects on hard cuts or impacts, or silence during reading holds. Music beat timing is unverified, and source reviews assessed visual frames only. Honor user audio and supplied assets, and do not invent them.
summary.assetRequirements: No source artwork, fonts, copy, or audio were supplied. Production needs separated spot-color layers, fixed ink-edge and paper textures, local fonts, and exact task copy. Motion references need actual phrase, punctuation, or approved-mark assets. Do not invent product copy or brand marks.
summary.combinations: Screen Printing alone suits bold flat-ink graphics. Motion Poster (style-103) adds a usable static poster and matched loops: compose the full poster first, and avoid gradients, constant headline motion, and mismatched loop endpoints. Silhouettes (style-043) suit narrative posters and title sequences: use dark ink with rust as the second plate, and avoid 043's slate accent and extra tonal layers.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default for composition, timing, validation, and export; Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists. SVG, with Canvas 2D as an alternative, owns flat-ink visuals. GSAP paused timelines drive motion, with optional Motion for one owner per property. Pillow or Sharp preprocess assets, and chroma-js checks contrast. Run check, snapshot, and render, then inspect frames and audio sync.
